# The pinned CI tools, one row per tool - installed by ./install.sh (through
# ./action.yml or ../setup-tools) and drift-checked by
# ../../scripts/check_tool_versions.sh. Both read it through ./lib.sh, so a
# tool pinned here cannot go unchecked.
#
#   name|pin|kind|url|verify|check|tag-prefix|sha256
#
# name        the tool's executable name, and what `tool:`/`tools:` inputs
#             name. install.sh finds it inside an archive by this name.
# pin         the version WITHOUT a leading "v"; the url carries a literal
#             "v" where upstream's tag or asset needs one.
# kind        raw      a bare executable (or script)
#             tar.gz   an archive searched for <name>; when it holds one build
#             tar.xz   per arch side by side, this machine's arch dir is kept
#             zip      an archive searched for <name>, the same way (needs unzip)
#             cmake    a source tarball built with cmake
#             make     a source tarball built with ./configure && make
#             Source kinds may append apt build deps: `cmake:libfoo-dev,libbar-dev`
#             (cmake always adds build-essential and cmake itself).
# url         %v is the pin. %a is this platform's asset slug, taken from the
#             sha256 column below - use it only with a per-platform sha256.
# verify      flags install.sh runs the installed tool with as a smoke test.
# check       where the drift check looks for newer releases:
#             github:<owner>/<repo>      releases API
#             gitlab:[<host>/]<project>  tags API; <project> url-encoded
#                                        (group%2Fname), host defaults to gitlab.com
#             npm:<package>              registry versions
#             -                          not drift-checked (say why above the row)
# tag-prefix  optional; what to strip off an upstream tag to get a pin. Blank
#             means an optional leading "v" (v1.2.3 and 1.2.3 both work); set
#             it when tags look like "<tool>-v1.2.3".
# sha256      required. The sha256 of the downloaded file (the raw binary, or
#             the archive before extraction) at this exact pin, one of:
#               <64 hex>
#                   one asset for every platform (a script, a source tarball,
#                   or a roster that only runs on one platform); url has no %a
#               <platform>[:<slug>]=<64 hex>,<platform>[:<slug>]=<64 hex>,...
#                   one asset per platform; <platform> is linux-x86_64,
#                   linux-aarch64, darwin-x86_64 or darwin-aarch64, and %a in
#                   the url becomes <slug> (default: the platform itself). A
#                   runner whose platform is not listed fails to install.
#             Example: `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` assets become
#               ...-%a.tar.gz|...|linux-x86_64:x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu=<hex>,linux-aarch64:aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu=<hex>
#             Compute each with `curl -sSfL <url> | sha256sum` (real %v/%a
#             substituted). It changes only in the commit that bumps `pin`; a
#             bumped pin with an unchanged sha256 is a red flag.
#
# Bumping a pin is a hand edit to one row: pin and sha256 together.
#
# Floating by design - tools this repo deliberately does not pin, and why.
# Each is still named here so "is this pinned?" has one place to look:
#
#   none. Tools pinned elsewhere, not floating: the Python tools (ruff,
#   basedpyright, zizmor, typos, pip-audit, shfmt-py) in the hashed
#   requirements-dev.txt, and markdownlint-cli2 and prettier in
#   ../../package-lock.json. Dependabot moves both.

# A fork of actionlint that accepts `uses: $/.github/actions/...` local refs, which upstream rejects.
